title: Quiz: Diagnostic Plots and Model Comparison

questions.text: In the Scale-Location diagnostic plot, what does a flat red loess line indicate?
options: The residuals have a mean of zero
The variance of residuals is approximately constant across fitted values (homoscedasticity)
There are no influential observations in the dataset
questions.explanation: Scale-Location plots the square root of standardised residuals against fitted values. A flat loess line means the spread of residuals is constant — the homoscedasticity assumption holds.

questions.text: Cook's Distance measures the influence of each observation on the fitted model. An observation with Cook's D > 1 is typically described as:
options: A statistical outlier with a large residual
An influential point that substantially changes the fitted coefficients when removed
An observation that violates the normality assumption
A leverage point that lies far from the centre of the predictor space only
questions.explanation: Cook's Distance combines residual size and leverage to measure how much the fitted model would change if that observation were removed. High D (>1 or >4/n) identifies influential points.

questions.text: AIC (Akaike Information Criterion) rewards models for fitting the data well but penalises them for having more parameters.
questions.explanation: AIC = -2·log(likelihood) + 2k, where k is the number of parameters. Lower AIC is better. The 2k penalty prevents adding parameters that do not meaningfully improve fit.

questions.text: gather_predictions(mod_a, mod_b) returns a data frame in what format?
options: One column per model, one row per observation
One row per model per observation, with a 'model' column and a 'pred' column
A list of two data frames, one for each model
A wide data frame with model names as column headers
questions.explanation: gather_predictions() stacks predictions from all models into a long (tidy) data frame with a 'model' column and a 'pred' column. This makes faceted ggplot2 comparisons straightforward.

questions.text: A Normal Q-Q plot shows that residuals deviate from the diagonal at both ends (heavy tails). The MOST important consequence is that:
options: The slope and intercept estimates are biased
Standard errors, t-statistics, and p-values may not be reliable for small samples
The model will fail to make any predictions
questions.explanation: OLS coefficient estimates (slope, intercept) are still unbiased under heavy-tailed noise — only the inference machinery (SEs, t-tests, CIs) relies on normality. For large samples, CLT provides approximate validity anyway.
